subject: Post-demo: on-prem peering gap analysis & action items
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@brightlane.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-21T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: on-prem peering gap analysis & action items

Hi Alex / Priya - thanks again for taking the demo today. Per our convo, I wanted to capture the immediate gaps we uncovered around the on-prem/VPN path for streaming inference and outline next steps so we can scope acceptance testing. TL;DR: Brightlane's latency tail and intermittent packet loss on the VPN are the biggest risks for meeting the 99th-percentile streaming SLO.

Summary of points from the call:
- Target SLOs: 95% < 120ms p99 for single-stream low-latency responses; concurrency target 150 simultaneous streams with sustained throughput of ~200 tokens/sec per stream.
- Current observed: Your pre-demo traces showed 180ms median p99 spikes to >350ms during brief bursts (see attachment).
- Path specifics: Traffic will exit Brightlane DC via customer-managed VPN to us-east-1 transit, then peer into Redwood Private edge for inference. Potential reordering at the VPN appliance during bursts was flagged by your network team.

Proposed immediate actions (owners & tentative windows):
1) Brightlane: run 24-hour pcap/latency sweep on the VPN appliance across peak windows and share traces (Alex). Target: 2027-09-23 end of day.
2) Redwood SE (Marissa): produce a peering test plan that covers UDP/TCP path behavior, MTU validation, and streaming keepalive tuning. Deliverable: peering-test-plan.pdf (attached). Target: 2027-09-22 COB.
3) Redwood SRE (Ben): prepare a lightweight probe harness that will simulate 150 concurrent streams with KV-caching pattern similar to your demo prompts; provide config snippets for the VPN appliance to allow steady flows (attached: vpn-config-snippets.txt). Target: 2027-09-24 test window.
4) Joint: agree on test acceptance criteria (latency percentiles, retransmit thresholds). Proposed acceptance: p95 < 80ms, p99 < 120ms, <0.1% packet loss over 15m windows.

Please reply with any corrections to the above and confirm Alex that your network team can commit to the trace upload by 09/23. If we can get that data, Marissa can start the test plan immediately and Ben will schedule the test harness.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0148

Attachments: peering-test-plan.pdf
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightlane.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@brightlane.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-21T17:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: on-prem peering gap analysis & action items

Thanks Sean — that matches what we discussed. Quick clarifications from our side:
- We can export full pcap and latency traces, but the network team asked if you prefer aggregated histograms + per-minute packet loss vs full pcap first. We can provide both, but pcaps will be large.
- The peak windows are typically 08:30-10:30 and 15:30-17:00 local (PST). We'll prioritize the test during those periods.
- We currently use an HA pair of VPN appliances (vendor: NetPathX) that do stateful failover; during failover events we've seen sequence reordering which aligns with your observation.

Confirming: we'll deliver aggregated histograms by EOD 2027-09-23 and can ship full pcaps if needed (estimate ~3GB/day).

Alex Turner
Infrastructure Ops Lead, Brightlane
alex.turner@brightlane.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightlane.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-22T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: on-prem peering gap analysis & action items

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and the window details. I attached a formal peering-test-plan (pdf) and included two short artifacts you requested: a CSV with the demo latency trace we captured (latency_trace_20270919.csv) and a compact VPN config snippet showing the keepalive and MSS settings we recommend (vpn-config-snippets.txt). Notes below on the practical testing approach.

Test plan highlights (high level):
- Objectives: validate path stability for streaming RPCs, confirm MTU/fragmentation handling, and reproduce the failover/reordering scenario at low concurrency and at target concurrency.
- Probe harness: we'll run a 3-phase run: (A) baseline single-stream to verify per-request RTT; (B) ramp to 150 concurrent streams over 20 minutes to capture warmup effects; (C) sustained 30m soak at target concurrency.
- Metrics to record: per-request latency histogram (1ms buckets), retransmits, out-of-order counts, CPU contended samples on the VPN appliance, and per-second token throughput.
- Acceptance thresholds: p95 < 80ms, p99 < 120ms, packet loss < 0.1% (15m). If we see transient p99 spikes tied to failover windows, we'll mark that as a conditional-fail and recommend HA config changes.

Preflight checklist for Brightlane network team:
1) Ensure management plane access so Ben's probe can initiate test flows from a Redwood test VM.
2) Allow the probe IP(s) through the VPN ACLs for the test window.
3) Export histograms and pcaps to the shared drive link after the run.

Proposed test window: 2027-09-24 08:30-10:30 PST (ramp at 08:30, soak at 09:00-09:30). Ben — can you confirm the harness scheduling?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightlane.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: on-prem peering gap analysis & action items

All — scheduling confirmed. I'll deploy the probe harness into our us-east-1 test tenancy and I'll need a one-hour window of VPN ACL changes for the probe IP range (details in vpn-config-snippets.txt). Plan: start 09/24 08:30 PST with a dry run for 15 minutes, then full ramp/soak. We'll stream live metrics to the shared dashboard; link posted to the Drive folder.

If Alex can drop the aggregated histograms by EOD today, I'll run a short pre-check against those numbers and adjust the harness pacing to better mimic Brightlane's traffic (token size distribution looks heavier than typical). If pcaps are easier for your team, go ahead and upload them — we have compressed storage.

Next steps checklist (final):
- Alex: upload histograms / pcaps to Drive by EOD 2027-09-23.
- Brightlane: permit probe IPs in ACL for 09/24 08:30-10:30 PST.
- Redwood (Marissa/Ben): run test, share live dashboard, and produce a short acceptance report within 24h of test completion.

Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
